text:
Step 0 of this study's protocol is complete and supplies its effective-df threshold. d_crit = 12 for PM/mKH, driven by n=80 reversed variances tau2=0 (rejection 7.44%, two-sided 99.9% Clopper-Pearson [0.0660, 0.0834]). Equal-subject HC3/Satterthwaite never left the upper band across 144 cells. 1,440,000 independent studies, zero nonfinite. Report and receipt: plsneuro/docs/verification/first-level-se-dcrit.md and first-level-se-dcrit.json.gz (SHA-256 22f10d80cc0e2a3bd27c384729bd819908ef6fb22186e18d072c6abd0895f295).

Executed with a Python reference PM/mKH validated against the 72 explicit native fixtures retained in docs/verification/group-controls-2026-09-08.json.gz: max absolute error 2.0e-10 estimate, 3.3e-11 SE, 7.8e-10 p, 6.3e-10 tau2, the p tolerance matching the one at which the native output agreed with metafor. It reproduces this repository's headline cell at 8.62% mean over five fresh seeds against the reported 8.85%. NATIVE CONFIRMATION OF d_crit IS OUTSTANDING AND BELONGS TO THIS TICKET: a validated reference locates a threshold, it does not qualify the provider. Re-running the ladder through GroupModel.mixedEffects / GroupEngine.fit is a small bounded task using the retained NativePmCalibration driver.

Two results that bear on the group work here, beyond the threshold. First, the failure is a cliff rather than a slope: every configuration is conservative from known variances down to df=50 and only inflates from df=25, so there is no gradual degradation to model. Second, the inflation is not purely a heterogeneity effect. With flat variances and no heterogeneity at all, rejection still reaches 7.62% at n=20 and 8.67% at n=80 by df=4. The controlled study varied df only at spread and reversed profiles and so could not show this; uncertainty in the weights inflates the test even when the true weights are equal. That is relevant to the joint effect-and-variance bootstrap research bd-01M21BNZR9ZBRAYY9JD5WCQ8KX, whose declared model should not assume the problem is confined to heterogeneous-variance designs.

Practical consequence for this study: d_crit=12 against a reported T - rank(X) in the low hundreds means the first-level effective df must collapse by more than an order of magnitude before group inference is affected. A modest shortfall is provably harmless, so the study's compute should be spent where a severe collapse is plausible: estimated voxelwise AR whitening, censoring, and inverse-covariance run pooling whose weights are data-estimated (FixedEffects.scala:382).
